what_it_does: Checks workstream ids, parent links and cycles, and the required and membership roles against the team lists in people.yml, returning a list of error strings whose work goes into one pass per workstream.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The three team sets depend only on people_data, but they are rebuilt inside the per-workstream loop, so with 60 workstreams the code builds them 60 times per call. Moving the block above the loop builds them once, and the loop body keeps the same membership tests on the same sets. Edge case to check in verify: with an empty workstreams list and a None people_data, the hoisted version raises where the original returned an empty list.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: parent_kind is assigned from id_to_workstream[parent_id] and never read. Removing the line drops one dict lookup and one .get per workstream that has a parent, which is about 40 of the 60 in workstreams.yml. Nothing can raise there, since parent_id was checked against id_to_workstream on line 99. The saving is expected to be negligible, and the measurement will say.

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: The chain walk is bounded by the parent depth, which is 2 at most in the current workstreams.yml (checked: 60 workstreams, maximum depth 2), so the cycle check costs about 120 dict lookups per call. A memo would add more code than it removes work.

what_it_does: Builds the README table rows for one group of SIGs, calling extract_row_data once per SIG and appending each row to a local string.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The second extract_row_data call for the same SIG sits in render_sig_details, which is called separately with only the ws. Removing the duplicate needs a shared value or a changed signature in two separate functions, so it cannot be one repair in one unit. The duplicated work is about 60 dict builds per run.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: content is a local variable with a single reference, so CPython performs the += in place and the concatenation is linear. This is the case verifying.md describes as already linear.

what_it_does: Builds the bulleted detail block for one SIG for sigs.md by calling extract_row_data and formatting each non-empty field.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Same duplicate as render_group line 157. The repair needs render_group and render_sig_details to share one computed value, which is an edit to two units. The work is about 60 dict builds per run, so the coupling is not worth it.

what_it_does: Turns a SIG heading into its GitHub anchor by stripping link syntax, lowercasing, removing non-alphanumeric characters and replacing spaces with hyphens.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The two patterns are string literals, and the re module caches compiled patterns by pattern string and flags, so each call after the first is a cache lookup, not a compile.

what_it_does: Reconciles the existing voter-notification comments with the roll file by removing stale @handle lines or deleting emptied comments, then posts new voters in batches, printing each action (or only printing it in dry-run mode).

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: For a comment with k stale handles, remove_handle_line runs one full regex pass over the body for each, so the body is scanned k times. One alternation pattern built from the stale handles removes the same lines in one pass. Lines matched by one handle's pattern are whole lines, and the trailing \s* only consumes blank lines, so removing them in one pass or k passes gives the same text. Sole caller of remove_handle_line is sync (line 147), so the helper can be left in place unchanged and the repair simply stops calling it.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: extract_mentions runs on the same body string twice per comment: once in the tagged loop at line 136 and again at line 145 on the same original. Reusing the list from line 136 removes one regex findall per comment. Line 157 scans new_body, which is a different string, so it stays.

what_it_does: Returns whether a comment body starts with the exact invitation header, by splitting the whole body into lines and comparing the first.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: str.splitlines also splits on \r, \x0b, \x0c, \x1c to \x1e, \x85, \u2028 and \u2029. A body whose first line holds one of those before any \n can give a different first line from body.split('\n', 1)[0], so a cheaper prefix test would not be identical on every input. Making it identical means reproducing splitlines' separator set. The saving is a split of one comment body of about 1 KB, a few microseconds.

what_it_does: Removes every line that is exactly `* @handle` (case-insensitively, with its trailing newline) from a body and returns the rest.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The compiled pattern is looked up in the re module cache on each call, keyed by the pattern string and flags. Each distinct handle is compiled once per process, and repeated calls for the same handle are cache hits. The per-call cost left is one cache lookup.

what_it_does: Looks up one GitHub login for a devstats name through the users API, sleeping 0.1 s before each request and returning the login or None.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The sleep is the rate-limit guard that the line's comment states. Removing it changes how fast the remote is asked, which can turn successful lookups into 403 responses, so the repair is not equivalent in the sense that matters here. It is a policy choice, not waste.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: requests.get without a Session opens a new TCP connection and TLS handshake for each username. A module-level requests.Session reuses the connection across calls, so each lookup after the first skips the handshake. Return values, headers and the sleep are unchanged. The only caller is build_devstats_rows (line 94), so the change is local.

what_it_does: Builds [login, contributions] rows by calling get_github_login for each devstats name in order and keeping the ones that resolve.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The only way to cut the wall time is to issue the lookups concurrently. That changes the request rate the 0.1 s sleep exists to limit, and it raises peak power while the requests overlap. It is not an equivalent edit of this unit.

what_it_does: Lists completed workflow runs in the window for each benchmark workflow, fetches each run's jobs, and keeps the bare-metal jobs with valid timing as records.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The bare-metal label is only visible on the jobs payload (line 100), so the filter cannot run before the per-run job fetch without changing which endpoint answers the question. Skipping runs in workflows that never use the label would change the records for workflows whose runs can use it. A repair of the request pattern is not one this machine can verify.

what_it_does: Runs `gh api --paginate` for one path in a subprocess and yields each JSON line of its output as a dict.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Replacing the subprocess with direct HTTP requests changes where the token comes from, since gh reads its own credential store. The edit is not one that keeps the behaviour of the function on the same machine, and any measurement of it needs the network.

what_it_does: Aggregates job records per (repository, workflow) for one window and renders them as a Markdown table sorted by total runtime.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The records list is walked once per window, and there are two windows, so the second walk is a pass over a few hundred records. The filter is the table's own work for its window, and merging the two passes would change render_table's shape for a saving well below the noise of the rest of the script.

what_it_does: Pages through a repo's issue comments since the cutoff and builds a per-user map of the PR and issue numbers each user commented on, caching it per repo.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `number not in commenters[user][kind]` scans a list on every comment, so for a user with n distinct numbers the cost is O(n) per comment and O(n squared) per user. A set of (user, kind, number) keys checked before the append gives O(1) membership. The lists in the returned dict keep their order and contents, so _check_comments and the debug output are unchanged. Sole caller is _check_comments (line 315), and the cache is read only here.

what_it_does: Scans a repo's cached issue events and returns, for each remaining user, the first event of the requested types they performed.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The loop keeps walking the whole event list after every user in remaining has been found. Breaking once len(found) equals len(remaining) returns the same dict, since found only ever holds members of remaining. Real saving is small, because most remaining users are inactive and the list is walked in full anyway.

what_it_does: Walks a user's candidate PRs in order and returns the first one whose reviews include a review by that user submitted on or after the cutoff.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The reviews list of one PR is fetched again for each user who has that PR as a candidate, within a batch and across the paginated path, and nothing caches it. A cache of reviews keyed by (repo, PR number) makes each PR cost one GET per run. The return value is the same, since the cache holds the same list the API returned.

what_it_does: Batches users ten at a time for a GraphQL first page of their reviewed PRs, verifies candidates through _verify_review_candidates, and paginates for users not yet confirmed.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The duplicate verification this would remove is the same fetch that the cache repair in _verify_review_candidates removes. Deduplicating the batch here would leave the per-user loop calling that unit, so the saving would come from the same reads. Rejected as a second repair for the same work.

what_it_does: Checks each triager against a repo's comments and label or close events and returns the set of users found active, short-circuiting across repos.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: debug() takes a finished string, so each f-string, including _fmt_numbers(numbers), is built for every active user even when DEBUG is False and debug() discards it. Guarding the three calls with `if DEBUG:` skips those builds and prints nothing differently with the flag off. The mechanism is string formatting per active user, which is small, so the saving is expected to be negligible.

what_it_does: Checks each approver against a repo's PR comments, issue comments and PR reviews in that order and returns the set of users found active.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The four debug f-strings are built even when DEBUG is False, including _fmt_numbers on each active user's numbers. Guarding them with `if DEBUG:` skips the formatting and keeps the output identical with the flag off. The saving is string formatting per active user, expected to be negligible.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: Merging the PR-comment and issue-comment passes into one would change the order of the debug lines printed when DEBUG is on, because PR-comment messages would no longer all come before issue-comment messages. The second pass over the same cached commenters is a dict lookup per remaining user. The output change alone rules it out.

what_it_does: Checks each maintainer against a repo's PR comments, issue comments, PR reviews, authored PRs and merge events, returning the set of users found active.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Six debug f-strings are built even when DEBUG is False. Line 650 also calls _extract_numbers on each authored result, so the number list is walked for a message that is discarded. Guarding the calls with `if DEBUG:` removes that work with the flag off and keeps the output identical with it on. The saving is expected to be negligible.

what_it_does: Adds a member entry to the Emeritus section of a README, creating the section if needed, and rewrites that section with its members sorted by display name.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The regex `^[-*+] \[` is applied to every section line twice: once in the list comprehension that builds member_lines (line 859) and again in the loop that finds first_member_idx and last_member_idx (lines 871 to 875). Both results can come from one loop over the lines, which saves a full regex pass over the section for every user added. The member_lines list, the indices and the rebuilt text are unchanged. Sole caller is create_emeritus_prs (line 1230).

what_it_does: Removes the line of one username from one README section and returns the new README, or None if the user is not in it.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The unit does one section search and one member match, and neither is repeated inside it. The repeated README searches come from create_emeritus_prs calling this once per user per role, which is a caller-side cost and not something this unit can change without changing create_emeritus_prs too.

what_it_does: For each repo with inactive members, fetches its README, removes each user from the role sections, adds them to Emeritus, then forks the repo, commits the README and opens or updates a pull request, or files a follow-up issue when the README needed no change.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: For each user and each of their roles, _find_section and _parse_members run again over the same README sections to look up a display name. Parsing each role section once per repo into a name map removes the repeated scans. The unit calls fetch_readme over the network first, so its inputs cannot be generated here.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: Each helper returns a new full copy of the README, a few tens of kilobytes, and a copy costs microseconds. The copies per repo are tens, against several HTTP calls per repo, so the saving is below anything the run can see.

what_it_does: Creates a fork of an upstream repo under the authenticated user if none exists, then waits until its git refs respond.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Moving the first check ahead of the 5 s sleep only saves time if the fork is already visible when the POST returns, and the code's own comment says fork git objects initialise asynchronously. Whether that happens is a property of GitHub's timing that this machine cannot measure, and the check cannot be made equivalent in its timing by any edit to this unit.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: A shorter or backed-off poll interval changes how often the remote is asked for refs. The fixed 5 s interval is a deliberate choice about remote load, not waste inside the function, and the repair would be a policy change rather than an equivalent edit.

what_it_does: Updates the body of an open cleanup issue with the same title if one exists, or creates it, after paging through the repo's open issues to look for it.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: A title search through the search API would be one request, but it answers from a separate index that can lag behind a just-opened issue, so it is not guaranteed to return the same result. The unit runs only when the README needed no change, which is rare, so the saving is small as well as uncertain.

what_it_does: Returns the number of the open move-to-emeritus PR for a repo by paging through its open PRs for the matching head branch, caching the result per repo.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The docstring at lines 714 to 715 says the search is by head branch name because the fork owner differs between local runs and CI. A head filter needs that owner, so the filter would miss PRs the current search finds. The walk is also cached per repo, so it runs once per repo.

what_it_does: Returns the start, end and header level of a named README section by matching its header and finding the next header of the same or higher level.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The f-string patterns are rebuilt each call, but they are identical strings, so the re module cache returns the compiled pattern after the first call. Only the string formatting remains, which is microseconds per section lookup.

what_it_does: Collects team members and repos for each role, checks activity per repo and maps it back to teams, prints the inactive report and, with --create-prs, calls create_emeritus_prs.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The repo list is fetched before the --repo filter is applied (line 1323 then 1326). The team's full repo list is what decides whether the team covers a requested repo, so skipping the fetch for a restricted run would change which teams are checked. Rejected as a change to the answer, not a saving of the same answer.
